story: Fort Mountain State Park is a forest in Georgia, USA, that covers 3,712 acres and was founded in 1938. It is named for an ancient 885-foot-long rock wall located on the peak. The park features a mixture of hardwood and pine forests, waterfalls, and a mountain lake.
matters: Situated in the Chattahoochee National Forest, the park provides a protected habitat for diverse wildlife such as black bears and white-tailed deer. Its forests and trails support a local decomposer community, plants, and various animal species.
name: Fort Mountain State Park
